web_evidence.title: And the Mountains Echoed: A Tale of Sibling Love and Hope
web_evidence.note: Scholarly structural analysis states that the novel has nine differently narrated chapters, an epistolary chapter, and chapters written in both first and third person.

web_evidence.title: And the Mountains Echoed Study Guide
web_evidence.note: Explicit whole-book overview identifies first-person Chapters 8 and 9, two document-based first-person chapters, and remaining third-person-limited chapters.

web_evidence.title: And the Mountains Echoed Study Guide
web_evidence.note: Point-of-view overview describes nine perspectives combining an epistolary chapter, a first-person chapter, and several third-person-limited chapters.

web_evidence.title: Review of And the Mountains Echoed
web_evidence.note: Contemporary newspaper review explicitly says some component stories use first person and others use third person, alongside a letter and interview.

web_evidence.title: And the Mountains Echoed
web_evidence.note: Authorized publisher excerpt confirms that the opening contains Saboor's locally embedded fable; its mixed speech and tale voices cannot alone establish the whole-book person.

search_log: Searched "And the Mountains Echoed" with point of view, first person, third person, narrator, chapters, and alternating narration.
Searched official author, Bloomsbury, Penguin Random House, and extract/first-chapter combinations; opened the Penguin Random House authorized opening and Bloomsbury reading guide.
Opened the UGC-listed journal article "And the Mountains Echoed: A Tale of Sibling Love and Hope" and verified its whole-book statement that chapters use first and third person.
Opened Course Hero, LitCharts, Dawn, and n+1 structural discussions; the first three explicitly corroborated the book's narration pattern.
Checked targeted passages for the embedded fable, Nabi's letter, Abdullah's note, Chapter 8, and Chapter 9 to distinguish constitutive narration from local speech and documents.

The Tampere University thesis established multiple narrators and plural perspectives but did not explicitly distinguish grammatical persons in its accessible abstract, so it was not used to support ALTERNATING.
person_note: The novel alternates sustained narration in different grammatical persons: substantial chapters use third-person narration, while Nabi's constitutive letter chapter and later narrators including Markos and Pari II use first person. The Tier B structural analysis independently states this first/third arrangement, and multiple explicit whole-book guides agree. First-person material local to Saboor's embedded fable, Nila's interview or poetry, character dialogue, and Abdullah's short note was not promoted to base narration. Remaining uncertainty concerns only the precise local attribution of a few clipped aphorisms, not the documented whole-book alternation.
